newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended slightly firmer on Monday after professional traders dominated a near deserted market for the entire session.

Dealers said institutional investors remained mostly sidelined after some bargain hunting in the early morning when prices were slightly lower, as most were waiting to get further clues on the overall market direction.

A row of strong economic data released since the latest 0.25 percent hike in U.S. interest rates has fuelled fears of another rise in May, keeping all market players alert for any additional signs of inflationary pressure in the United States, they said.
"We all expect a hike (in U.S. interest rates) in May," one dealer said.
He said the size of the hike remained unclear.
US March CPI figures are due on Tuesday.

Analysts expect both the overall index and the core figure, excluding the volatile food- and energy components, to show a 0.3 percent increase on a monthly basis. Year-on-year, they foresee a 3.0 percent rise.
Dealers said the Dutch bond market attributed more importance to the U.S. data than to the German ifo business climate index, also due this week.

They said volume was thin in all maturities, adding private investors seemed to have turned away from the bond to the share market, while institutional investors remained inactive until they had a clearer picture of the prospects for Dutch bonds.

"There are no moves along the curve, there's no switching with Germany. As long as the market is waiting for clues and opinions are divided, it will remain very very quiet over here," one dealer said.
